ai_logs_output: return the GPU Redfish status/processor JSON so the user confirms GPU health state is reported.

ai_commands: -- Set NTP server: set the BMC NTP server sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -X PATCH -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"NTPServers":["<ntp>"]}' "https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/1/NetworkProtocol" 2>&1 2>&1" using a user-designated NTP server; state-changing, then verify with ipmitool -I lanplus -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" mc info 2>&1.
ai_packages_needed: curl + BMC creds + reachable NTP server address
ai_logs_output: return the PATCH response + the BMC time/sync read so the user confirms the NTP server was set and the BMC time synced to it.
risk: RISK: pointing BMC at a wrong/offline NTP can drift time; use the user-designated NTP and confirm reachability first.

ai_commands: -- Create VLAN ID: create a VLAN on the NIC via sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ip link add link eth0 name eth0.100 type vlan id 100; ip link set eth0.100 up 2>&1; ip addr add 192.168.100.2/24 dev eth0.100 2>&1 2>&1"; state-changing network config on the DUT.
ai_logs_output: return the full `ip -d link show eth0.100` + `ip addr show eth0.100` so the user confirms the VLAN device (id + tagged interface) was created and up.
risk: RISK: adding a VLAN IP can disrupt DUT networking; use a dedicated test VLAN id/range and confirm it does not collide with the management VLAN.

ai_commands: -- Ping same VLAN ID: ping between two hosts on the same VLAN: on the DUT sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ip link add link eth0 name eth0.100 type vlan id 100 2>&1; ip addr add 192.168.100.2/24 dev eth0.100 2>&1; ping -c5 192.168.100.3 2>&1 2>&1"; needs a peer host on the same VLAN.
ai_packages_needed: iproute2 + iputils-ping + a peer host behind the same switch VLAN
ai_logs_output: return the ping response + loss% so the user confirms same-VLAN hosts reach each other without errors.
risk: RISK: requires a peer host + switch VLAN config; confirm topology before running.

ai_commands: -- Ping different VLAN ID: verify an untagged/tagged peer on a different VLAN does NOT reach the DUT unless routed: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ip link add link eth0 name eth0.200 type vlan id 200 2>&1; ip addr add 192.168.200.2/24 dev eth0.200 2>&1; ping -c5 192.168.100.3 2>&1 2>&1"; result depends on switch inter-VLAN routing.
ai_logs_output: return the ping result + which VLAN (tag) each interface has so the user confirms the expected reachability behaviour for cross-VLAN traffic.
risk: RISK: cross-VLAN reachability depends on the switch/router config; confirm expected outcome with the user before judging pass/fail.

ai_commands: -- Remove VLAN ID: remove the VLAN device sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ip link del link eth0 name eth0.100 type vlan id 100 2>&1; ip link del eth0.100 2>&1; ip addr show 2>&1 | grep -A2 vlan; echo done 2>&1"; state-changing cleanup.
ai_logs_output: return the delete command output + a final `ip -d link show` confirming the VLAN interface is gone / the eth0 link is back to normal.
risk: RISK: deleting a VLAN also drops any IP bound to it; confirm no active connection depends on it.

ai_commands: -- Configuring BMC Network through IPMI for static(IB): set the BMC network to a static IP (IB) via IPMI ipmitool -I lanplus -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" lan set 1 ipsrc static 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" lan set 1 ipaddr 192.168.0.50 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" lan set 1 netmask 255.255.255.0 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" lan print 1 2>&1 | grep -iE "IP Address|Subnet Mask|IP Source"; state-changing network setting.
ai_logs_output: return the final `ipmitool lan print` (ip source = static + the new IP/netmask) so the user confirms the BMC static IP was applied.
risk: RISK: changing the BMC IP drops the current out-of-band channel; keep a console/serial path and restore the original IP after.

ai_commands: -- Configuring BMC Network through IPMI for dhcp(IB): set the BMC network back to DHCP (IB) via IPMI ipmitool -I lanplus -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" lan set 1 ipsrc dhcp 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" lan print 1 2>&1 | grep -iE "IP Address|IP Source"; state-changing.
ai_packages_needed: ipmitool + BMC creds + working DHCP for the BMC
ai_logs_output: return the final `ipmitool lan print` (ip source = dhcp + the DHCP-assigned IP if present) so the user confirms the BMC DHCP config was restored.
risk: RISK: switching to DHCP requires a valid DHCP server on the BMC network; a lease failure leaves the BMC IP stale.

ai_commands: -- AC lost: AC-lost (power loss) test requires physically removing AC power and observing the response (power-policy + crash-free recovery); human-only AC handling.

ai_commands: -- Health Check on UBB and OAM: health-check UBB and OAM0-7 via Redfish Chassis from BMC SSH. Load amdgpu first sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "modprobe amdgpu 2>&1 2>&1"; then query UBB sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Chassis/UBB 2>&1" and each OAM sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "for OAM in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Chassis/OAM_$OAM; echo; done 2>&1 2>&1".
ai_packages_needed: amdgpu kernel module (present on GPU driver stack) + curl
ai_logs_output: return the full Redfish Chassis JSON for UBB and OAM0-7 so the user confirms Health=OK, HealthRollup=OK, State=Enabled for each.

ai_commands: -- SMC Reset and Set DateTime: force-reset the SMC and set DateTime via Redfish Manager/AMC from BMC SSH: POST ForceRestart sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -X POST http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Managers/AMC/Actions/Manager.Reset -d "{\"ResetType\":\"ForceRestart\"}" 2>&1" then ping for boot sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ping -c 4 192.168.31.1 2>&1 2>&1" then read Manager/AMC for the time/date sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Managers/AMC 2>&1"; setting DateTime is a state write.
ai_logs_output: return the ForceRestart POST response, the ping boot result, and the Manager/AMC JSON (DateTime) so the user confirms the SMC restarted and time is synced with BMC.
risk: RISK: SMC ForceRestart briefly resets the UBB baseboard management controller; may cause a short OOB gap - do not run during any active test.

ai_commands: -- Log Collection: collect SMC/system logs via Redfish LogServices from BMC SSH: list LogServices sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices 2>&1" then dump EventLog entries sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" 'http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Systems/UBB/LogServices/EventLog/Entries' >> event.log 2>&1; wc -l event.log 2>&1".
ai_logs_output: return the LogServices list + the saved event.log (full SMC EventLog entries) so the user confirms no error/abnormal entries are present.

ai_commands: -- Power Management: manage the Power Limit Watts for UBB/OAM via OOB Redfish from BMC SSH plus in-band ROCm: first read the current EnvironmentMetrics SetPoint for each OAM sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "for OAM in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" http://192.168.31.1/redfish/v1/Chassis/OAM_$OAM/EnvironmentMetrics; echo; done 2>&1 2>&1"; the actual power-limit set uses ROCm/power-cap tooling and is a state write.
ai_logs_output: return the EnvironmentMetrics SetPoint (current Max Power Limit) for each OAM so the user confirms the value; the power-capping write is done via rocm-smi and judged against the Max Power Test criteria.
risk: RISK: changing GPU power capping affects thermal/power behaviour of the OAM modules; do not auto-run, apply with careful intent and reset afterwards.

ai_commands: -- GPU Thermal Test: GPU thermal test on the AMD UBB/OAM. Load driver and read per-OAM thermal via ROCm sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "modprobe amdgpu 2>&1; rocm-smi --showtemp 2>&1 2>&1" and observe under load; the full thermal soak run is long and needs the vendor stress recipe.
ai_logs_output: return rocm-smi --showtemp (per-sensor junction/mem temperature) so the user confirms temperatures are within the thermal limits during the test.
risk: RISK: long thermal test sustains high load/temperature; ensure cooling and monitor temps; do not auto-run without a temperature-safe setup.

ai_commands: -- Max Power Test: Max Power test on the AMD UBB/OAM. Measure peak power under full GPU load via ROCm power API sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "rocm-smi --showpower 2>&1 2>&1" and compare against the power cap; needs a load generator + the vendor Max Power recipe.
ai_packages_needed: rocprof/rocm-smi (ROCm) + a GPU power load tool
ai_logs_output: return rocm-smi --showpower per-GPU power readings during full load so the user confirms peak power meets the Max Power pass criteria.
risk: RISK: Max Power test runs GPUs at full load; monitor power/thermal closely and do not auto-run without the approved load recipe.

ai_commands: -- Install OS sheet-B (Secure Boot enabled): install Windows Server with Secure Boot/TPM on the SUT. Agent can pre-check the secure-boot state from OS sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "bootctl status 2>&1 | grep -iE "secure boot|setup mode"; mokutil --sb-state 2>&1 2>&1"; the OS install itself needs the Windows ISO + interactive setup (BIOS F1, RAID driver loading) performed by an operator.
ai_packages_needed: Windows Server ISO + install media; mokutil (for pre-check)
ai_logs_output: return the pre-install secure-boot status (SecureBoot state + Setup Mode) so the user confirms CSM disabled / Secure Boot Standard Mode before install; the OS install evidence (drivers without error, confirm-SecureBootUEFI result) is collected by the operator.
risk: RISK: OS install wipes the boot disk; do not auto-run without an approved ISO and backup of the current OS.

ai_commands: -- ROT(PFR) FW Flash (ROT/PFR FW): flash the ROT PFR firmware via the SF600 flash tooling. Agent can verify post-flash SUT status from OS sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -t 2>&1 | tail -n 30; echo "---system status---"; uptime; lspci 2>&1 | wc -l 2>&1"; the ROT PFR flash itself uses the vendor SF600 tool + signed image and is a firmware write.
ai_packages_needed: SF600 ROT flash tool + signed PFR image (user-provided)
ai_logs_output: return the post-flash system status (dmesg tail, uptime, device count) so the user confirms the SUT is stable after the ROT(PFR) FW flash succeeded.
risk: RISK: flashing ROT/PFR firmware is destructive; only use the approved SF600 image and never auto-run during production.

ai_commands: -- Security mode: change the ROT security mode. Agent can only read current state from OS sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "mokutil --sb-state 2>&1; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -iE "rot|pfr|secure" | tail -n 20 2>&1"; the security-mode change requires the TPM physical-presence jumper/switch and BIOS F1 setup navigation by an operator.
ai_logs_output: return the current secure-boot/ROT-related dmesg lines so the user confirms the state before an operator changes the ROT security mode in BIOS.
risk: RISK: ROT security-mode change needs physical TPM-presence assertion + BIOS setup - operator required; do not auto-run.

ai_commands: -- TPM enabled: check the TPM is enabled in BIOS then verify the TPM device is visible in OS. Agent can verify the OS-side presence sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ls -la /dev/tpm* 2>&1; lspci 2>&1 | grep -i tpm; [ -e /sys/class/tpm/tpm0 ] && echo "TPM present" || echo "TPM absent" 2>&1" ; the BIOS enable step is done by an operator in the Security setup page.
ai_logs_output: return the /dev/tpm* listing + lspci TPM grep + sys TPM flag so the user confirms TPM device should exist on the OS side.

ai_commands: -- TPM disbled: disabling TPM is done in the BIOS Security/TPM setup page by an operator; the agent can only check OS-side TPM absence after it is disabled sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ls -la /dev/tpm* 2>&1; lspci 2>&1 | grep -i tpm; [ -e /sys/class/tpm/tpm0 ] && echo "TPM present" || echo "TPM absent" 2>&1".
ai_logs_output: return the /dev/tpm* listing + lspci TPM grep + sys TPM flag so the user confirms TPM device should NOT exist on the OS side.

ai_commands: -- PCIe ACS_Status: read PCIe ACS status. Agent scans each root-port/switch for the ACS capability sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "for d in $(lspci -D | awk "{print \$1}"); do lspci -s $d -vvv 2>/dev/null | grep -A3 -i "ACSCtl" | grep -iE "ACSCtl" | sed "s/^/dev $d /"; done 2>&1 | grep -iE "SrcValid|ACSCtl" 2>&1"; an ACS-enabled port shows SrcValid+ and disabled shows SrcValid-.
ai_logs_output: return the ACSCtl lines per PCIe device (SrcValid+/-) so the user confirms which devices have ACS enabled/disabled in OS.

ai_commands: -- MSI-X status: read PCIe MSI-X status for each device sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "for d in $(lspci -D | awk "{print \$1}"); do lspci -s $d -vvv 2>/dev/null | grep -q "MSI-X" && echo "dev $d: $(lspci -s $d -vvv 2>/dev/null | grep -A2 "MSI-X" | grep "Enable")"; done 2>&1 2>&1"; reports MSI-X Enable+/- per device.
ai_logs_output: return the per-device MSI-X Enable status so the user confirms MSI-X is enabled on the expected devices.

ai_commands: -- Check AMI Armor Register: read the AMI Armor register values. Agent reads the OS-visible SMBIOS/BCP info sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ls /sys/firmware/efi/efivars/ 2>&1 | grep -i armor; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -i armor | tail -n 10 2>&1"; the register read (AMI RU tool / UEFI Shell `pci 0 14 3` at 0x000000A0 = FF FF FF FF) must be done in the pre-OS AMI RU/UEFI Shell by an operator.
ai_logs_output: return the OS-visible armor-related info + the operator must provide the RU/pci register dump (FEC10000 = FF, addr 0xA0 = FF FF FF FF) so the user verifies against the AMI Armor guide.

ai_commands: -- SMM TSEG Range should cover the entire SMM region: requires a debug BIOS from the BIOS RD team + reading IO Space register 0xB2 under the AMI RU tool and watching the BMC SOL terminal to confirm SmiHandler4 is skipped; all pre-OS/BIOS-RD-only, the agent cannot obtain the debug BIOS nor inspect SMM from the OS SSH session.
ai_packages_needed: debug BIOS + AMI RU tool + BMC SOL console (operator/RD)
ai_logs_output: operator flashes the debug BIOS, opens SOL, reads 0xB2 register and records the SMI handler list (SmiHandler3/5/6 present, SmiHandler4 skipped); agent cannot produce this evidence.

ai_commands: -- SRIOV enable: verify SR-IOV. Agent can check the IOMMU/SR-IOV capabilities in OS sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lspci 2>&1 | grep -i "virtual function"; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -iE "iommu|sriov" | tail -n 10; cat /sys/bus/pci/devices/*/sriov_totalvfs 2>/dev/null 2>&1"; enabling SR-IOV in BIOS + configuring the hypervisor is done by the operator.
ai_logs_output: return the OS-side virtual-function device count + sriov_totalvfs + IOMMU dmesg lines so the user confirms the SR-IOV VFs appear in the guest/host inventory.

ai_commands: -- AMISCE linux: use AMISCE linux under OS to export/import BIOS settings. Agent runs the export/import sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "./SCELNX_64 /o /s cfg.txt 2>&1; echo "---import---"; ./SCELNX_64 /i /s cfg.txt 2>&1 2>&1" then reboot and verify in setup; requires the AMISCE SCELNX_64 binary copied to the DUT first.
ai_logs_output: return the SCELNX export/import stdout (should state Script file exported/imported successfully) so the user confirms the saved BIOS configuration round-trips.
risk: RISK: importing BIOS settings writes the BIOS NVRAM config; ensure the cfg.txt contains the intended settings and backup the current config before import.

ai_commands: -- Check NUMA code configure: after the operator sets the BIOS NPS (NPS1/2/4), agent verifies the NUMA node allocation in OS sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lscpu 2>&1 | grep -E "^NUMA|Socket|Core|On-line"; echo "---node memory---"; numactl --hardware 2>&1 | grep -i node 2>&1".
ai_logs_output: return lscpu NUMA lines + numactl --hardware node map so the user confirms the NPS setting yields the expected node allocation (NPS1 node0~1, NPS2 node0~3, NPS4 node0~7).
risk: RISK: changing NPS in BIOS is an operator action; the agent only reads the resulting NUMA layout.

ai_commands: -- Check AC Loss Control status: set the AC-loss power policy via IPMI-OOB so it matches BIOS. Agent sets the policy ipmitool -I lanplus -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" chassis policy always-off 2>&1 and reads back ipmitool -I lanplus -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" chassis status 2>&1 | grep -i "Last Power Event"; confirming the BIOS AC Loss Control page matches the OOB setting is done in the BIOS setup by an operator.
ai_logs_output: return the ipmitool chassis policy set output + Last Power Event status so the user confirms the OOB policy matches the BIOS AC Loss Control setting.
risk: RISK: setting power policy affects behaviour after AC loss; the operator verifies the BIOS page matches and resets the policy after each check.

ai_commands: -- Check  BERT/ERST/HEST under OS: check BERT/ERST/HEST error record tables under OS sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg 2>&1 | grep -iE "BERT|ERST|HEST|ACPI Error" ; ls /sys/firmware/acpi/tables/ 2>&1 | grep -iE "BERT|ERST|HEST" 2>&1".
ai_logs_output: return the dmesg lines mentioning BERT/ERST/HEST + the /sys/firmware/acpi/tables listing so the user confirms the error source record tables are present under OS.

ai_commands: -- Crash BMC and recovery: crash-and-recover the BMC by cutting AC power mid-firmware-update to simulate a crash, then verifying the BMC auto-reverts to the previous stable firmware. Requires a person to physically cut/restore AC power and an operator to drive the two BMC firmware flashes; the agent cannot simulate the power interruption nor boot the BMC flash recovery console.
ai_packages_needed: BMC firmware images + human AC power control + BMC recovery procedure
ai_logs_output: operator performs the two firmware flashes with the intentional AC cut at the second update, re-applies AC and records the revert to the previous firmware + normal BMC boot; agent cannot produce this evidence.
risk: RISK: crashing the BMC mid-flash and AC-cycling is physically destructive to the BMC firmware state; human-only, perform carefully on a test unit.

ai_commands: -- Leaky Bucket Setting in BIOS menu: editing the ECC Leaky Bucket Threshold in the BIOS memory menu requires BIOS setup access; the agent cannot enter the BIOS setup page from the OS SSH session.
ai_logs_output: operator sets the Leaky Bucket Threshold in BIOS, saves+resets, and the BMC SEL should log the behaviour; agent cannot drive the BIOS menu.

ai_commands: -- 2nd DIMM error injection - all channel: 2nd DIMM error injection across all channels uses the BIOS leaky-bucket ECC test path (BIOS menu setup + register check) and verifies DIMM_B still triggers logs on the system + BMC SEL; the injection and BIOS interaction cannot be done from the OS SSH session.
ai_packages_needed: BMC SEL + BIOS setup / memory RAS tool (operator)
ai_logs_output: operator performs the 2nd-DIMM error injection and collects the system log + BMC SEL entries so the user confirms DIMM_B still raises the error; agent cannot inject the hardware ECC error.
risk: RISK: memory error injection may log real RAS events; operator-driven, not auto-run.

ai_commands: -- Swap CPUs: swapping the physical CPUs requires a person to perform the CPU socket exchange on the motherboard; the agent cannot swap CPUs over SSH. After the swap the agent can verify the CPU identity sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lscpu 2>&1 | grep -E "Model name|Socket|Core"; dmidecode -t 4 2>&1 | grep -iE "Version|Socket Designation" 2>&1".
ai_logs_output: operator performs the CPU swap + power-on; agent returns lscpu/dmidecode CPU info so the user confirms BIOS+OS detect the correct swapped CPU.
risk: RISK: CPU swap is physical hardware work - human only; agent must not attempt.

ai_commands: -- AMIPRD: AMIPRD runs in the BIOS UEFI Shell (pre-OS) and dumps the performance record to txt/csv for RD review; the agent cannot enter the UEFI Shell from the OS SSH session.
ai_logs_output: operator boots the UEFI Shell, runs AMIPRD.efi, and uploads the Performance Record Dump report (txt+csv) for RD review; agent cannot drive the pre-OS shell.

ai_commands: -- Check system boot time(AC on and warm/cold reboot): measure boot time. Agent can measure OS-to-ready boot time via systemd-analyze sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "systemd-analyze 2>&1; systemd-analyze blame 2>&1 | head -n 10 2>&1"; the BIOS-setup-entry warm/cold reboot timing needs an operator to record the moment the setup menu appears.
ai_logs_output: return systemd-analyze total/kernel/userspace boot time and top startup units so the user can compare against the <4 min warm-boot target; the setup-entry timing is recorded by the operator.

ai_commands: -- Early video output: early video output timing needs a person to power-cycle the system (incl unplugging all AC cables) and visually observe the moment video appears within 5 seconds; the agent cannot toggle AC power or see the display output over SSH.
ai_packages_needed: human at the machine + a display/monitor
ai_logs_output: operator powers on/AC-cycles and records whether video output appears within 5 seconds; agent cannot observe the display.
risk: RISK: AC power unplug/re-plug is a physical power action - human only.

ai_commands: -- WOL function test: WOL function test. Agent (as the wake client from the peer host) sends the magic packet sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ethtool $DUT_NIC 2>&1; echo "client sends magic packet"; ether-wake -i $DUT_NIC $DUT_MAC 2>&1 2>&1"; the SUT must be in S5 (graceful shutdown), which needs an operator to set S5/WOL in the OS+BIOS and to unplug/re-plug AC for the disable case.
ai_logs_output: return the ether-wake magic-packet send result + the ping/WOL wake status so the user confirms the system wakes when WOL is enabled and does not when disabled; operator handles the S5/AC steps.
risk: RISK: WOL test requires shutting the SUT to S5 and AC unplug/re-plug - operator steps; do not auto-run over a needed connection.

ai_commands: -- SY.2_CPU Motherboard (SY.2_CPU Motherboard): validate the CPU motherboard per CPU-vendor guidance; agent runs the generic platform health sweep sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lscpu 2>&1 | grep -E "Model name|Socket|Core"; dmidecode -t 4 2>&1 | grep -iE "Version|Manufacturer"; lspci 2>&1 | grep -iE "VGA|Processing accelerators" 2>&1".
ai_logs_output: return the CPU model/socket/core count + dmidecode processor version + accelerator enumeration so the user confirms the CPU motherboard is populated and recognised.

ai_commands: -- CPU Temperature: read the HMC CPU average temperatures via D-Bus introspection on the BMC sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.EntityManager /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/bmc/HMC_0/M0_CPUTempAvg0 2>&1; echo "---"; busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.EntityManager /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/bmc/HMC_0/M1_CPUTempAvg0 2>&1 2>&1".
ai_logs_output: return the full busctl introspect output for M0_CPUTempAvg0 and M1_CPUTempAvg0 so the user confirms the CPU temperature objects exist and respond with the configured settings.

ai_commands: -- Linpack(HPL): run the AMD HPL Linpack benchmark. The AMD HPL tarball (hpl.tar.bz2) install script builds all prerequisites and needs internet + a freshly installed Ubuntu 20.04+; after the AMD HPL package is installed, the agent runs the benchmark and collects Gflops.
ai_packages_needed: AMD HPL (hpl.tar.bz2 - AMD-provided) + internet at install + build toolchain gcc/gfortran/BLAS
ai_logs_output: return the HPL run output (problem size, N,NB,P,Q,time, Gflops) so the user compares the achieved Gflops against the Intel/AMD spec.
risk: RISK: HPL runs at high CPU load for a long time; ensure adequate cooling and run in a maintenance window.

ai_commands: -- SW.1_System software: run the NVSSVT system-software qualification suites (L0/L1). The agent can collect the software/OS inventory that NVSSVT validates sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "nvidia-smi 2>&1 | head -n 12; echo "---"; uname -r; cat /etc/os-release 2>&1 | grep -E "PRETTY_NAME" 2>&1"; the full NVSSVT suite is a multi-test vendor-run needing the NVSSVT package.
ai_packages_needed: NVSSVT (NVIDIA tool - install first) + NVIDIA driver/container stack
ai_logs_output: return the pre-run inventory (driver version, kernel, OS) + the NVSSVT suite pass-rate so the user confirms the 100% NVSSVT pass target; exact suite command discussed after install.

ai_commands: -- SW.1_NVSSVT (GB SW.1_NVSSVT): complete the L0/L1 NVSSVT suites per the Grace SBIOS/FW references. Agent can dump the software stack to qualify sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "cat /etc/os-release 2>&1 | grep PRETTY_NAME; uname -r 2>&1; ls /sys/firmware/ 2>&1; nvidia-smi 2>&1 | head -n 8 2>&1"; running the full qualification needs the NVSSVT tool.
ai_logs_output: return the OS/kernel/firmware inventory that NVSSVT qualifies + the suite pass-rate result so the user confirms the 100% target.

ai_commands: -- SW.2_Server RAS Capability: run the NVRAS server-RAS-capability suites. Agent first collects the RAS-relevant OS state sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "rasdaemon --help 2>&1 | head -n 5; ls /sys/devices/system/edac/ 2>&1; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -iE "ras|edac" | tail -n 10 2>&1"; the full NVRAS validation needs the NVIDIA NVRAS tool suites.
ai_logs_output: return the RAS-related dmesg/edac inventory + the NVRAS suite pass-rate so the user confirms the 100% NVRAS pass target.

ai_commands: -- SW.2_NVRASTool (GB SW.2_NVRASTool): complete the NVRASTool suites per the Grace RAS catalogs. Agent collects the in-OS RAS state sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ls /sys/bus/edac/ 2>&1; rasdaemon --status 2>&1; dmesg -l err 2>&1 | tail -n 20 2>&1"; the NVRASTool suite is a vendor multi-test run.
ai_logs_output: return the RAS/EDAC inventory + dmesg error tail + the NVRASTool pass-rate so the user confirms GPG 100% NVRAS pass target.

ai_commands: -- SW.3_Debug Log Collection: follow NVDebug procedures to capture all logs in-band and OOB. Agent can trigger the in-band log capture tooling sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "nvdebug 2>&1 | head -n 20 2>&1"; the full NVDebug log collection uses the NVIDIA NVDebug tool (NVOnline 1109504).
ai_logs_output: return the NVDebug in-band capture stdout + the list of collected log files (in-band + OOB) so the user confirms all logs are captured without issues.

ai_commands: -- SW.3_NVDebug Tool (GB SW.3_NVDebug): run NVDebug to collect both in-band and OOB logs. Agent runs the in-band collection sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "nvdebug 2>&1 | head -n 20; echo "---OOB logs dir---"; ls -la /var/log 2>&1 | grep -i debug 2>&1"; requires the NVIDIA NVDebug tool.
ai_logs_output: return the NVDebug in-band stdout + the collected OOB log file listing so the user confirms the 100% NVDebug pass rate.

ai_commands: -- SW.4_DOCA Performance (SW.4_DOCA Performance): run the NVNetPerf test suites to qualify DOCA networking performance. Agent can pre-check the DOCA/network stack sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "docactl --version 2>&1; ethtool -i $DUT_NIC 2>&1 | head -n 6; ibstat 2>&1 | grep -iE "state|link" 2>&1"; the NVNetPerf suite is a long benchmark needing the vendor test setup.
ai_logs_output: return the DOCA/network inventory + the NVNetPerf suite results so the user confirms they meet the networking configuration criteria.
risk: RISK: NVNetPerf runs long network benchmarks; needs the full DOCA/SmartNIC topology and setup, not a one-liner.

ai_commands: -- DG.1_Partner Field Diagnostics (Level 2): run the partner Field Diagnostics Level 2: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "./partnerdiag --field --level2 --run_on_error --no_bmc 2>&1 | tail -n 40 2>&1"; requires the NVIDIA partnerdiag package placed on the DUT.
ai_logs_output: return the partnerdiag field-level2 output (per-item PASS/FAIL) so the user confirms all items pass without system hang or reboot.
risk: RISK: partnerdiag runs low-level HW diagnostics incl NVLink/PCIe; run in a maintenance window and do not interrupt.

ai_commands: -- Field RMA Diagnostics: run the GB field RMA diagnostics (Python-based, supported kernels listed). Agent runs the diagnostic executable sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "./diagnostic 2>&1 | tail -n 30 2>&1"; requires the RMA diagnostic package on the DUT (Ubuntu22.04/RHEL9.2/SLES15SP5 kernels).
ai_packages_needed: NVIDIA field-RMA diagnostic package (user-provided); Python 3.10 + glibc 2.12+
ai_logs_output: return the diagnostic exit code + the printed PASS/FAIL/RETEST marker so the user confirms the hardware passes (0/PASS) or sees the FAIL/RETEST reason.

ai_commands: -- DG.2_Partner Manufacturing Diagnostics (HGX DG.2 Partner Mfg Diagnostics): run sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "./partnerdiag --mfg --run_spec=spec_blackwell-hgx-8-gpu_partner_mfg.json --run_on_error --no_bmc 2>&1 | tail -n 40 2>&1"; requires the HGX partnerdiag package on the DUT.
ai_logs_output: return the partnerdiag manufacturing output (per-item PASS/FAIL) so the user confirms all items pass without system hang/reboot.
risk: RISK: manufacturing diagnostics exercise all HW (NVLink/GPUs/PCIe); long run - maintenance window only.

ai_commands: -- Partner Diagnostics (GB Partner Mfg Diagnostics): cd to the diag directory and run sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "./partnerdiag --mfg --run_spec=spec_cx8aas_board_partner_mfg.json 2>&1 | tail -n 40 2>&1" ; requires the GB partnerdiag package.
ai_logs_output: return the partnerdiag manufacturing output (PASS/FAIL/RETEST printed at end) so the user confirms the hardware passes manufacturing.
risk: RISK: manufacturing diag exercises the board hardware; run in a maintenance window.

ai_commands: -- NL.1_NVLink enumeration and full NVLink fabric topology: NVQual Test #9 enumerates NVLink + the full fabric topology. Agent first dumps the current topology sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "nvidia-smi nvlink -s 2>&1; nvidia-smi topo -m 2>&1 2>&1"; the full NVQual #9 topology run needs the NVQual suite.
ai_logs_output: return the nvidia-smi nvlink -s (link status) + topo -m (matrix) output + the NVQual #9 result so the user confirms the full NVLink fabric topology passes.

ai_commands: -- NL.2_NVLink bandwidth: NVQual Test #9 measures NVLink bandwidth. Agent first samples the link counters sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "nvidia-smi nvlink -sc 2>&1 | head -n 20; nvidia-smi -q -d NVLINK 2>&1 | head -n 40 2>&1"; the NVQual #9 bandwidth test is a benchmark run.
ai_logs_output: return the NVLink counter/bandwidth sample + the NVQual #9 result so the user confirms NVLink bandwidth passes.
risk: RISK: NVQual #9 runs a heavy NVLink throughput test; do not co-run other GPU workloads.

ai_commands: -- US.1_USB2.0 Interface between HMC and BMC: verify the HMC-BMC USB2.0 link enumerates to high speed. Agent checks the USB tree for the HMC management port sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lsusb -t 2>&1; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -iE "usb 2-?[0-9]|SuperSpeed|high-speed usb" | tail -n 20 2>&1".
ai_logs_output: return the lsusb -t tree + the USB high-speed enumeration dmesg lines so the user confirms the HMC-BMC USB2.0 link enumerates at high speed.

ai_commands: -- SP.1_SPI functional - BMC and BMC EROT: verify SPI on the QSPI0 bus between the BMC and the CEC1736 BMC EROT. This is a physical bus-level (logic analyser/scope) or BMC-internal EROT firmware check the agent cannot perform over SSH.
ai_logs_output: operator validates the QSPI0 BMC-BMC-EROT communication and records the successful SPI handshake; agent cannot measure the physical bus.

ai_commands: -- SPI.2_SPI functional - CPU and TPM: verify SPI on CPU QSPI1 to the TPM. This is a physical bus-level check (scope/logic analyser or TPM-firmware handshake) not reachable from the OS SSH session by the agent.
ai_logs_output: operator validates the CPU QSPI1-TPM SPI communication and records it; agent cannot measure the physical bus.

ai_commands: -- UA.1_UART CPU to USB-C: verify UART CPU-to-USB-C connectivity. Agent can enumerate the USB-C serial adapters sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg 2>&1 | grep -iE "cp210x|ftdi|usb 1-" | tail -n 15; ls /dev/ttyUSB* /dev/ttyACM* 2>&1 2>&1"; a functional send/receive traffic loop needs a physical USB-C connection.
ai_logs_output: return the dmesg serial-adapter probe + the /dev/ttyUSB*/ttyACM* list so the user confirms the CPU UART enumerates to the USB-C port; the traffic loop is judged by the operator.

ai_commands: -- UA.2_UART BMC to USB-C: verify UART BMC-to-USB-C connectivity. Agent lists the serial devices under BMC sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ls /dev/ttyS* /dev/ttyUSB* 2>&1; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -iE "serial|ttyS|usb" | tail -n 12 2>&1"; a send/receive loop needs an operator on the USB-C console.
ai_logs_output: return the BMC serial device listing + dmesg probe lines so the user confirms the BMC UART is present on the USB-C port; traffic test judged by operator.

ai_commands: -- UA.3_UART HMC to USB-C: verify UART HMC-to-USB-C. Agent checks the HMC serial/console device state sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ls /dev/ttyACM* /dev/ttyUSB* 2>&1; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -iE "acm|usb" | tail -n 12 2>&1"; a bidirectional UART traffic test needs a physical terminal on the USB-C connector.
ai_logs_output: return the USB-C serial device listing + dmesg probe lines so the user confirms the HMC UART is present; the send/receive evidence is captured by the operator.

ai_commands: -- DOCA Installation: install DOCA (host repo + doca-runtime/sdk/tools + sshpass/numactl/ipmitool). Agent installs the repo package then the DOCA packages sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "sudo dpkg -i doca-host-repo-*_amd64.deb 2>&1; sudo apt-get update -y 2>&1; sudo apt install -y doca-runtime doca-sdk doca-tools sshpass numactl ipmitool 2>&1 | tail -n 20 2>&1"; requires the DOCA host repo deb + internet.
ai_packages_needed: doca-host-repo deb + doca-runtime doca-sdk doca-tools sshpass numactl ipmitool
ai_logs_output: return the dpkg -i + apt install output (tail) so the user confirms prerequisites and DOCA packages install without error and the DPU device ID matches SPEC.

ai_commands: -- DPU Connection: check the BlueField DPU connection sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "update-pciids 2>&1; lspci 2>&1 | grep -i BlueField; lspci -s $(lspci 2>/dev/null | grep -i BlueField | head -1 | cut -d" " -f1) -vvv 2>&1 | head -n 30 2>&1".
ai_logs_output: return the lspci BlueField line + the -vvv detail (device/vendor ID, speed) so the user confirms the DPU matches the SPEC definition.

ai_commands: -- Firmware Flash & Check (Firmware Flash & Check): check rshim, then install a new BFB + flash DPU firmware, reboot, verify. Read the DPU state first sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "systemctl status rshim 2>&1 | head -n 8; ls /dev/rshim0/ 2>&1; cat /dev/rshim0/misc 2>&1 2>&1"; the BFB install + firmware flash is a destructive DPU write needing the BFB image.
ai_logs_output: return the rshim status + the /dev/rshim0 contents + misc + the pre-flash DPU FW version so the user confirms the state before the BFB/firmware flash; the flash and bfvcheck result are judged after the write.
risk: RISK: installing a new BFB and flashing DPU firmware overwrites the DPU OS/firmware; use the approved BFB image and never auto-run during production.

ai_commands: -- Driver Installation: install the MLNX-OFED driver. Agent mounts the MLNX ISO and runs mlnxofedinstall sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "mkdir -p /tmp/mst 2>&1; mount MLNX_Packages/MLNX_OFED_LINUX-5.8-1.1.2.1-ubuntu22.04-x86_64.iso /tmp/mst 2>&1; cd /tmp/mst && yes | ./mlnxofedinstall --force 2>&1 | tail -n 20 2>&1"; requires the MLNX-ISO on the host and a reboot afterwards.
ai_logs_output: return the mlnxofedinstall output (tail) so the user confirms the driver installed without error; after reboot the agent runs mst start / mst status -v to list MLNX devices.
risk: RISK: MLNX-OFED install can change the networking driver stack and needs a reboot; do not auto-run on a machine with active traffic.

ai_commands: -- Firmware Flash: flash the MLNX firmware via flint. Agent reads the current FW then flashes sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "mst start 2>&1; flint -d mlx5_0 q 2>&1 | grep -iE "FW Version|Device ID" 2>&1" -> flash sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "flint -d mlx5_0 -y -i MLNX_FW.bin -ocr b 2>&1; echo "---after---"; flint -d mlx5_0 q 2>&1 | grep -i "FW Version" 2>&1"; needs the correct FW bin for the device.
ai_logs_output: return the pre-flash and post-flash flint FW version lines so the user confirms the firmware flashed without error and the new version is correct.
risk: RISK: flashing NIC firmware can brick the device on failure; use the exact FW bin matched to the device PSID and never auto-run.

ai_commands: -- LED Check: physical LED check on the Ethernet port (Activity blinks green, Link Up solid green) is a visual inspection only a person at the machine can perform.
ai_packages_needed: human at the machine (visual LED check)
ai_logs_output: operator visually confirms the Ethernet port LED behaviour (activity=blinking green, link-up=solid green) and records photos; agent cannot see the LEDs.

ai_commands: -- Link Flap: repeat Ethernet link up/down 5x per port and ping the port IP. Agent toggles the interface sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do ip link set $DUT_NIC down; sleep 2; ip link set $DUT_NIC up; sleep 3; ping -c2 -W2 $PEER_IP 2>&1 | tail -n 2; done 2>&1 2>&1" ; needs an idle NIC + a peer IP.
ai_logs_output: return the 5 ping results per flap so the user confirms the NIC works when link-up and drops when link-down and is still normal after 5 flaps.
risk: RISK: bringing the NIC down interrupts the SSH/network that may carry the agent connection; use the management NIC or a maintenance window.

ai_commands: -- LED Check: physical InfiniBand LED check (physical up = solid yellow) is a visual inspection only a person at the machine can perform.
ai_packages_needed: human at the machine (visual LED check)
ai_logs_output: operator visually confirms the InfiniBand port LED (solid yellow when physical link up) and records photos; agent cannot see the LEDs.

ai_commands: -- Link Flap: repeat InfiniBand link up/down 5x and check ibstat physical state. Agent brings the mlx IB interface up/down and reads the state sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do ip link set ib0 down; sleep 2; ip link set ib0 up; sleep 3; ibstat 2>&1 | grep -iA10 "mlx" | egrep "mlx|state"; done 2>&1 2>&1" ; needs an IB interface and driver.
ai_logs_output: return the 5 ibstat Physical-state lines (LinkUp when up / Disabled when down) so the user confirms the IB port still works after 5 flaps.
risk: RISK: bringing the IB interface down interrupts IB traffic; ensure no active fabric-critical traffic.

ai_commands: -- LED Check: physical management-LAN LED check (green/yellow states per link/activity) is a visual inspection only a person at the machine can perform.
ai_packages_needed: human at the machine (visual LED check)
ai_logs_output: operator visually confirms the management-LAN LED behaviour (link off/on/activity per criteria) and records photos; agent cannot see the LEDs.

ai_commands: -- Link Flap: repeat the DPU management-LAN link up/down on the DPU OS and ping the port IP. Runs inside the DPU SSH session sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do ip link set $MGT_NIC down; sleep 2; ip link set $MGT_NIC up; sleep 3; ping -c2 -W2 $PEER_IP 2>&1 | tail -n 2; done 2>&1 2>&1" ; DPU SSH (ubuntu@OOB_IP) + a peer IP required.
ai_logs_output: return the 5 ping results per management-LAN flap so the user confirms the mgmt NIC works up, drops down, and is still normal after 5 flaps.

ai_commands: -- Assembly Check - Cable (Cable): assembly check - components easy to plug/unplug + still detected after a plug cycle requires a person to physically plug/unplug the Cable at the machine; the agent cannot handle physical components.

ai_commands: -- Assembly Check - Board (Board): assembly check - components easy to plug/unplug + still detected after a plug cycle requires a person to physically plug/unplug the Board at the machine; the agent cannot handle physical components.

ai_commands: -- Check PCIe: check the ConnectX-7 PCIe device ID, vendor ID, speed and bandwidth sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lspci -nn 2>&1 | grep -i "Mellanox\|15b3"; lspci -s $(lspci -nn 2>/dev/null | grep -i "Mellanox\|15b3" | head -1 | cut -d" " -f1) -vvv 2>&1 | grep -iE "LnkCap|LnkSta|DeviceName|Device" 2>&1".

ai_commands: -- Check MST & ibstat: check MLNX devices and link status with and without connection. Agent runs sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "mst status -v 2>&1 | grep -iE "MST|mlx|ConnectX"; echo "---ibstat with loopback---"; ibstat 2>&1 | grep -iA10 "mlx" | egrep "mlx|state" 2>&1"; requires MFT and loopback of the MLNX ports (physical).
ai_logs_output: return mst status -v device list + the ibstat physical-state lines so the user confirms the MLNX information shows correctly with and without connection.

ai_commands: -- Check the floating point value: measure GPU floating-point performance with clpeak. Agent installs and runs it sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "apt-get install -y clpeak 2>&1 | tail -n 5; clpeak 2>&1 | head -n 60 2>&1"; requires the GPU driver + OpenCL runtime.
ai_logs_output: return the clpeak output (single/double FP throughput, integer, memory bandwidth, latency) so the user matches the values against the GPU spec.

ai_commands: -- Performance: evaluate GPGPU performance by training Minigo. Agent can pre-check the GPU/training env sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "nvidia-smi 2>&1 | head -n 12; which python3; pip list 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "tensorflow|pytorch|jax" 2>&1"; the Minigo training run needs the Minigo repo + dataset + a long training session.
ai_logs_output: return the pre-run GPU/toolkit inventory + the Minigo training throughput so the user compares the NV score versus the official MLPerf NV score.
risk: RISK: Minigo training is long-running and compute-heavy; run in a maintenance window with GPU cooling.

ai_commands: -- Multi - Node - NCCL: run multi-node NCCL. Agent does the setup (hosts, password-free ssh, OpenMPI deps) then the NCCL allreduce on 2 nodes sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "apt-get install -y libpmix-dev libfabric-dev libev-dev zlib1g-dev 2>&1 | tail -n 3; mpirun --hostfile /etc/hosts -np 2 /path/nccl-tests/build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 128M -f 2 2>&1 | tail -n 15 2>&1"; requires 2 SUT nodes + NCCL-tests + OpenMPI.
ai_logs_output: return the mpirun all_reduce_perf output (busbw/algBW per size) so the user confirms the multi-node NCCL runs without error and meets the NVIDIA performance doc spec.
risk: RISK: multi-node NCCL needs 2 hosts in the cluster with password-free SSH + full GPU bandwidth; not a one-liner, requires the cluster set up first.

ai_commands: -- Testing Inter-device Bandwidth: measure inter-GPU (xGMI) bandwidth on the AMD platform. Agent installs rocm-bandwidth-test and runs it sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "rocm-smi 2>&1 | head -n 15; apt-get install -y rocm-bandwidth-test 2>&1 | tail -n 3; rocm-bandwidth-test 2>&1 | grep -iE "xGMI|read|write|b/w" | head -n 30 2>&1"; requires latest ROCm.
ai_logs_output: return the rocm-bandwidth-test inter-device (xGMI) read/write bandwidth results so the user matches them against the AMD GPU spec.

ai_commands: -- Ethernet Performance (src=BlueField-DPU): run iPerf Ethernet throughput for 5 min. Agent starts the server and a client run sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "iperf -s -i 60 & sleep 2; iperf -c $SERVER_IP -i 60 -t 300 2>&1 | tail -n 12; kill %1 2>/dev/null 2>&1" ; requires a second host as the iperf peer.
ai_logs_output: return the 5-minute iperf throughput summary (per-60s interval + final average) so the user confirms the Ethernet bandwidth matches the NIC SPEC during stress and the system stays workable afterwards.

ai_commands: -- Infiniband Performance (src=BlueField-DPU): run ib_write_bw InfiniBand throughput for 5 min. Agent checks CRC errors before/after the run sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ethtool -S $DUT_NIC 2>&1 | egrep -i "crc|err" | head; echo "---run---"; ib_write_bw -d mlx5_0 -t 300 2>&1 | tail -n 12; echo "---after---"; ethtool -S $DUT_NIC 2>&1 | egrep -i "crc|err" | head 2>&1" ; needs a peer IB node.
ai_logs_output: return the CRC-error counters before/after + the ib_write_bw 5-min result so the user confirms the IB bandwidth matches SPEC and there are no CRC errors after stress.

ai_commands: -- Ethernet Performance (src=ConnectX-NIC): run iPerf Ethernet throughput for 5 min. Agent starts the server and a client run sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "iperf -s -i 60 & sleep 2; iperf -c $SERVER_IP -i 60 -t 300 2>&1 | tail -n 12; kill %1 2>/dev/null 2>&1" ; requires a second host as the iperf peer.
ai_logs_output: return the 5-minute iperf throughput summary (per-60s interval + final average) so the user confirms the Ethernet bandwidth matches the NIC SPEC during stress and the system stays workable afterwards.

ai_commands: -- Netperf: run Netperf (TCP/UDP) throughput. Agent builds netperf from the HP github tarball and runs sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "tar -zxf netperf-netperf-2.7.0.tar.gz 2>&1; cd netperf-2.7.0 && ./configure >/dev/null 2>&1 && make >/dev/null 2>&1 && make install >/dev/null 2>&1; netserver & sleep 2; netperf -t TCP_STREAM -H $SERVER_IP -l 60 -P 0 2>&1 | tail -n 8; kill %1 2>/dev/null 2>&1" ; needs a peer host as netserver.
ai_logs_output: return the netperf TCP_STREAM thruput result so the user matches it against the NIC spec.

ai_commands: -- Iperf: run iperf3 throughput. Agent installs iperf3 and runs server/client sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "apt-get install -y iperf3 2>&1 | tail -n 3; iperf3 -s & sleep 2; iperf3 -c $SERVER_IP -P 4 -t 60 -i 10 --logfile /tmp/iperf.txt 2>&1; kill %1 2>/dev/null; tail -n 15 /tmp/iperf.txt 2>&1" ; needs a peer host.
ai_logs_output: return the iperf3 4-stream 60s output (interval + final sum) so the user matches the throughput against the NIC spec.

ai_commands: -- Perftest: run Perftest (ib_write_bw/ib_read_bw) over InfiniBand. Agent sets up IPoIB modules and runs the test sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "modprobe ib_ipoib; modprobe ib_uverbs; modprobe rdma_ucm; ib_write_bw -d mlx5_0 2>&1 | tail -n 10 2>&1" ; needs OFED + a peer IB node + IPoIB configured.
ai_packages_needed: OFED + libibverbs + infiniband-diags + a 2nd IB host
ai_logs_output: return the perftest ib_write_bw result so the user matches the InfiniBand throughput against the NIC spec.

ai_commands: -- AC Cycle 1000 times: AC power-cycle the SUT 1000 times over 48 hrs. The AC power on/off must be driven by a person or a PDU the agent cannot control; the agent can run the post-boot check after each cycle sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "uptime 2>&1; dmesg -l err 2>&1 | tail -n 20; lspci 2>&1 | wc -l 2>&1" and can read BMC SEL via ipmitool to confirm no errors.
ai_packages_needed: human/PDU for AC power control + ipmitool (SEL read)
ai_logs_output: return the per-cycle boot uptime + dmesg error tail + device count so the user confirms no device loss and then reads the BMC SEL to confirm no error info across the 1000 AC cycles.
risk: RISK: AC power cycling is physically disruptive (1000 power cuts); needs a person/PDU at the machine, never auto-run via the agent.

ai_commands: -- 10 times: AC-drop the SUT 10 times while stressing CPU/DIMM/HDD. The agent runs the stress load before each drop sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "stress-ng --cpu 0 --vm 2 --hdd 1 -t 5m 2>&1 | tail -n 5 2>&1" but the physical AC cable drop/re-plug must be done by a person at the machine.
ai_logs_output: return the stress run output + the post-restore boot status (uptime + dmesg tail) so the user confirms the system works normally and the BMC/SEL displays the AC-drop log after re-plug.
risk: RISK: AC cable drop/re-plug is physical power work - human only; do 10 cycles carefully with PSU stress in mind.

ai_commands: -- Reboot 500 times (Stability - Cold Reboot, cold (AC-off between boots)): reboot the SUT 500 times over 12 hrs. The agent issues each reboot sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "sync && systemctl reboot 2>&1 2>&1" and after each boot re-runs the health check sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "uptime; dmesg -l err 2>&1 | tail; lspci 2>&1 | wc -l 2>&1"; the reboot-loop control and cold (AC-off between boots) handling needs a reboot controller script + operator supervision.
ai_logs_output: return the per-boot health output (uptime/errors/device count) so the user confirms no hang, no blue screen and no device loss across the 500 reboots; BMC SEL read via ipmitool confirms no log errors.
risk: RISK: 500 reboots interrupt all services for 12 hrs; run in a dedicated maintenance window.

ai_commands: -- Reboot 500 times (Stability - Warm Reboot, warm (AC stays on)): reboot the SUT 500 times over 12 hrs. The agent issues each reboot sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "sync && systemctl reboot 2>&1 2>&1" and after each boot re-runs the health check sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "uptime; dmesg -l err 2>&1 | tail; lspci 2>&1 | wc -l 2>&1"; the reboot-loop control and warm (AC stays on) handling needs a reboot controller script + operator supervision.
ai_logs_output: return the per-boot health output (uptime/errors/device count) so the user confirms no hang, no blue screen and no device loss across the 500 reboots; BMC SEL read via ipmitool confirms no log errors.
risk: RISK: 500 reboots interrupt all services for 12 hrs; run in a dedicated maintenance window.

ai_commands: -- Idle 24 hrs: idle the SUT for 24 hrs with hibernate disabled. Agent disables hibernate/suspend sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "systemctl mask sleep.target suspend.target hibernate.target hybrid-sleep.target 2>&1; echo "hibernate disabled" 2>&1" then lets the system idle; after 24 hrs the agent collects the idle logs + checks the RTC/clock drift.
ai_logs_output: return the masking confirmation + the post-idle system/bmc log error check so the user confirms no error/hang during the 24-hr idle; a timed drift check verifies the clock did not drift.

ai_commands: -- Full-Loading Stress with Full-Config(2700W): full-loading stress with full config (2700W, 4 PSU). Requires a physical full-config unit + 4 PSUs + human MAC revision; the agent can run the software stress mix (CPU/Disk/Memory/GPU/Networking) sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "stress-ng --cpu 0 -t 8h 2>&1 | tail -n 3 & nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,power.draw --format=csv 2>&1; fio --name=write --size=1G --rw=write --runtime=60 2>&1 | tail -n 3 2>&1" ; the full 8-hr concurrency + PSU power draw is judged by the operator.
ai_packages_needed: stress-ng + fio + nvidia-smi (+ GPU NVQual/IB stress stack)
ai_logs_output: return the concurrent stress output (stress-ng/fio/nvidia-smi power+utilization) so the user confirms CPU/Disk/Memory/GPU/Network stay loaded for 8 hrs with no errors; MAC + PSU setup is done by the operator.
risk: RISK: 2700W full-load stress is long and power-hungry; needs a full-config unit + 4 PSU and adequate cooling - operator setup, do not auto-run.

ai_commands: -- BurnIn 48 hrs Stress (GPU/CPU/Memory/HDD/Network stress): BurnIn 48-hrs stress of GPU/CPU/Memory/HDD/Network. Agent copies the BurnInTest tool and starts it on the CPU module sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "cp BurnInTest* /opt/ 2>&1; cd /opt && (./bittcp64 -c 48h 2>&1 | tail -n 10) & sleep 5; uptime 2>&1" ; the 48-hr full-load window + Task-manager verification is done by the operator.
ai_logs_output: return the BurnInTest launch + the running process/uptime so the user confirms CPU/Memory/Network are under full load for 48 hrs with a clean BurnIn/BMC/System log afterwards.
risk: RISK: 48-hr BurnIn is a long high-load run; operator schedules it and supervises the task-manager loading; not a quick one-liner.

ai_commands: -- Ethernet Stress: run the IB read/write tool over Ethernet for all CX7 and BF3 ports for 1 hour. Agent runs the throughput test sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "for p in $ETH_PORTS; do ib_read_bw -d $p -t 3600 2>&1 | tail -n 5; done 2>&1 2>&1" ; after stress the agent checks CRC/error counters sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ethtool -S $DUT_NIC 2>&1 | egrep -i "crc|err" | head -n 10 2>&1" ; needs OFED/IB tools.
ai_logs_output: return the 1-hr ib_read_bw results per port + the post-stress CRC/error counters so the user confirms the Ethernet bandwidth matches SPEC and the event log has no error after stress.

ai_commands: -- Infiniband Stress: run the IB read/write tool over InfiniBand for all CX7 and BF3 ports for 1 hour. Agent runs sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "for p in $IB_PORTS; do ib_read_bw -d $p -t 3600 2>&1 | tail -n 5; done 2>&1; echo "---crc after---"; ethtool -S $DUT_NIC 2>&1 | egrep -i "crc|err" | head -n 10 2>&1" ; needs OFED/IB tools + a peer IB node.
ai_logs_output: return the 1-hr ib_read_bw results per port + the post-stress CRC/error counters so the user confirms no unexpected error after the InfiniBand stress.
risk: RISK: 1-hr IB stress saturates the fabric; run in a maintenance window and monitor the IB ports.

ai_commands: -- XGMI Receiver Margin Search Test: XGMI receiver margin search via amdxio. Agent runs the link-status check then the margin search sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "sudo ./amdxio -xgmi -linkstatus 2>&1 | tail -n 20; echo "---margin---"; sudo ./amdxio -margin -xgmi -all -ber=10 -errcnt=5 2>&1 | tail -n 30 2>&1"; requires the amdxio tool + the AMD margin recipe.
ai_logs_output: return the amdxio linkstatus + margin search output and the generated xgmi_4PT_margin_all*.csv (rows = lanes tested) so the user judges PASS per the UI/Volt/Margin columns.
risk: RISK: XGMI margining drives the GPU interconnect at the receiver edge; run in a maintenance window and do not co-run other GPU load.

ai_commands: -- XGMI 4 Point Screen Test: XGMI 4-point screen test via amdxio. Agent runs the link status then the 4pt screen test on all links sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "sudo ./amdxio -xgmi -linkstatus 2>&1 | tail -n 20; echo "---4pt---"; sudo ./amdxio -margin -xgmi -all -ber=10 -errcnt=5 -4pt -phaseleftrange=2:0.2 -phaserightrange=2:0.2 -dactoprange=4:0.4 -dacbotrange=4:0.4 2>&1 | tail -n 30 2>&1"; requires amdxio.
ai_logs_output: return the amdxio 4pt screen-test CSV (56 links x 16 lanes = 896 rows for -all) so the user confirms each offset ErrCnt column is <=5 and offsets match the test parameters.
risk: RISK: the XGMI 4pt screen sweep stresses the interconnect margins; maintenance-window only, no other GPU load concurrently.

ai_commands: -- CPU over temperature via peltier device / remove heatsink: physically remove or heat the CPU heatsink with a peltier device to drive TCritical and verify shutdown + SEL over-temp entry. A physical/environmental fault-injection the agent cannot perform.
ai_logs_output: operator heats the CPU / removes the heatsink to reach TCritical, confirms shutdown, SEL over-temp entry and LED; agent cannot inject over-temp.

ai_commands: -- Using Not Support CPUs: install unsupported CPUs of the same type and confirm the system does not boot and the BMC/uEFI SEL logs an unsupported-CPU configuration. Requires physically swapping in non-supported CPUs, which the agent cannot do.
ai_logs_output: operator installs the unsupported CPUs, boots and checks no-boot + BMC/uEFI SEL unsupported-CPU entries; agent cannot physically swap CPUs.

ai_commands: -- Mismatched CPUs: install two mismatched CPUs and confirm the system does not boot and logs an unsupported-CPU-configuration entry. Requires physically swapping in mismatched CPUs, which the agent cannot do.
ai_logs_output: operator installs mismatched CPUs, boots and checks no-boot + SEL unsupported-CPU entries; agent cannot physically swap CPUs.

ai_commands: -- Using Not Support DIMMs: install unsupported DIMMs and confirm the system does not boot and the BMC/uEFI SEL logs an unsupported-DIMM configuration with the lightpath pointing at the failing DIMM. A physical DIMM swap the agent cannot do.
ai_logs_output: operator installs unsupported DIMMs, boots and checks no-boot + SEL + lightpath/fault light; agent cannot physically swap DIMMs.

ai_commands: -- Mismatched DIMMs: install two types of mismatched DIMMs and confirm the system does not boot and the logs an unsupported-DIMM configuration. A physical DIMM swap the agent cannot do.
ai_logs_output: operator installs mismatched DIMMs, boots and checks no-boot + SEL unsupported-DIMM entry; agent cannot physically swap DIMMs.

ai_commands: -- Power On via BMC WebUI: confirm the system is off, then power it on via the BMC. Agent can issue the same power-on over IPMI/Redfish sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ipmitool -I lanplus -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis power on 2>&1; sleep 5; ipmitool -I lanplus -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis power status 2>&1 2>&1" ; the BMC-WebUI click itself is a GUI action the agent cannot drive, but the power-on is reproducible via API.
ai_packages_needed: ipmitool (power-on via API; WebUI click is operator)
ai_logs_output: return chassis power on/status output so the operator confirms the system powers on without error and the event log has no error.
risk: RISK: power-cycling the SUT interrupts OS state; operator-approved window only.

ai_commands: -- Sensors - Sensor: read the BMC hardware-sensor list and confirm all sensor info matches SPEC. Agent can dump the full SDR/sensor list via ipmitool sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ipmitool -I lanplus -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr elist 2>&1 | head -n 80; echo "---sensor list---"; ipmitool -I lanplus -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sensor list 2>&1 | head -n 60 2>&1" .
ai_logs_output: return the ipmitool sdr elist + sensor list so the operator confirms all sensor info matches SPEC.

ai_commands: -- System Inventory: read the BMC system inventory (system/processor/memory/baseboard/power/thermal/PCIe/storage/network). Agent can pull most of it via IPMI/Redfish sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ipmitool -I lanplus -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" fru print 2>&1 | head -n 60 2>&1" ; the full GUI inventory view (BMC WebUI per-category) is operator-read for the visual confirmation.
ai_logs_output: return the ipmitool fru print so the operator confirms the data is readable and correct across all inventory categories.

ai_commands: -- InfiniBand Performance: run ib_write_bw (ConnectX) against a peer for 5 minutes and confirm bandwidth meets SPEC with no error. Agent can launch the one-sided BW test sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ib_write_bw -a -d mlx5_0 --report_gbits -q 8 -s 1048576 -t 300 2>&1 | tail -n 25; ibstat 2>&1 | head -n 20 2>&1" ; requires a second IB node running ib_write_bw in server mode and the mlx5 driver/ib-utils installed.
ai_packages_needed: mlx5 driver + infiniband-diags/ib_write_bw + peer IB server
ai_logs_output: return the ib_write_bw throughput (Gb/s) + ibstat so the operator confirms bandwidth matches SPEC and the system event log has no error after stress.
risk: RISK: sustained 5-min IB traffic saturates the link; run in a maintenance window.

ai_commands: -- NIC internal mechanical check: physically install the NIC in each supported PCIe slot and check for mechanical issues. A physical insertion/mounting check the agent cannot perform.
ai_logs_output: operator installs the NIC into all supported slots and confirms no mechanical issues; agent cannot physically install hardware.

ai_commands: -- NIC device information in BIOS: boot into BIOS, open the network page and confirm the NIC info + firmware is correct. A BIOS setup-menu read the agent cannot drive.
ai_logs_output: operator opens the BIOS network page and confirms NIC info + firmware are correct; agent cannot enter BIOS setup.

ai_commands: -- NIC device information in OS: read the NIC info + firmware under the OS. Agent can dump it sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lspci -nn 2>&1 | grep -Ei "Ethernet|Infiniband|Network"; ip link 2>&1 | head -n 40; for d in /sys/class/net/*; do [ "$(basename $d)" = lo ] && continue; ethtool -i "$(basename $d)" 2>&1 | head -n 8; break; done 2>&1" ; confirm info + firmware are correct.
ai_logs_output: return lspci NIC line + ip link + ethtool -i driver/firmware so the operator confirms NIC info + firmware are correct.

ai_commands: -- E.1s FW Update: check the NVMe E1.S firmware revision then flash the new image. Agent can read the current FW sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "nvme id-ctrl /dev/nvme0n1 2>&1 | grep -E "fr|mn" 2>&1" and, with the image + approval, issue the download/activate sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "sudo nvme fw-download /dev/nvme0n1 --fw=/home/user/e1s_fw.bin 2>&1; sudo nvme fw-activate /dev/nvme0n1 --slot=1 --action=1 2>&1 2>&1" ; flashing is a firmware write on a storage device.
ai_logs_output: return nvme id-ctrl pre-flash FW, then post-flash FW after activate+reset so the operator confirms the update succeeds and the version matches the bin.
risk: RISK: NVMe firmware flash is destructive; only with the approved image in an operator-approved window, backup data first.

ai_commands: -- LED Check: physically observe the storage-device LED (solid green when powered, blinking green during activity). A physical LED inspection the agent cannot see.
ai_packages_needed: physical sight of the storage LED (operator)
ai_logs_output: operator observes the storage LED color/state per SPEC; agent cannot visually inspect the LED.

ai_logs_output: no concrete procedure/criteria in the workbook; needs the referenced E1S board spec steps + expected result.

ai_commands: -- PDB_BD: the workbook gives only "follow up spec procedure / criteria" - no concrete steps or expected results. Cannot be executed or classified without the referenced external spec.
ai_logs_output: no concrete procedure/criteria in the workbook; needs the referenced PDB board spec steps + expected result.

ai_commands: -- Type 46 - String Property: run dmidecode --type 46 to read the SMBIOS Type 46 (String Property) table. A pure read sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmidecode --type 46 2>&1; echo "---exit $?---" 2>&1" ; confirm info matches SPEC.
ai_logs_output: return the full dmidecode --type 46 output so the operator confirms the string properties match SPEC.

ai_commands: -- LTSSM (PCIe Link Margin): follow the Intel Server System Validation Manual for link margin behavior. Requires the Intel validation/margin tooling and hardware setup, an operator/lab activity the agent cannot drive.
ai_logs_output: operator runs the Intel LTSSM margin flow per the validation manual and compares behavior to the specification; agent has no Intel tooling.

ai_commands: -- Stress 4 hrs (-5% 5V/3.3V): run BurnInTest under a temperature chamber profile (0C/40C ramps) and then confirm no error for 4 hours. Environmental chamber + Windows BurnInTest operation the agent cannot control.
ai_logs_output: operator runs the chamber profile + BurnInTest for 4 hrs and confirms no error/hang/BSOD in BurnIn/BMC/system logs; agent cannot drive the chamber.

ai_commands: -- Stress 4 hrs (+5% 5V/3.3V): run BurnInTest under the +5% margin temperature chamber profile and confirm no error for 4 hours. Environmental chamber + Windows BurnInTest operation the agent cannot control.
ai_logs_output: operator runs the +5% chamber profile + BurnInTest for 4 hrs and confirms no error/hang/BSOD; agent cannot drive the chamber.

ai_commands: -- Uboot flash: plug the BMC UART console and flash the BMC image through the uBoot TFTP/sf flow. The flash steps are done over the physical BMC UART console by an operator; the agent can only help stage the image and verify the BMC responds afterwards sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ipmitool -I lanplus -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc info 2>&1 | grep -Ei "Firmware Revision" 2>&1" .
ai_packages_needed: BMC UART console + TFTP server + BMC image (operator)
ai_logs_output: operator runs the uBoot tftp/sf update on the BMC UART, reboots the BMC and confirms it flashes successfully; agent verifies BMC responds + FW revision after.
risk: RISK: flashing the BMC via UART is destructive and can brick the BMC; operator-only with the approved image.

ai_commands: -- Debugport flash: change the debug-port jumper, flash the BMC encrypted ROM via the AST2600 uart_fw_py tool, then restore the jumper. A physical jumper + UART flashing flow done by an operator; the agent can only verify the BMC comes back sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ipmitool -I lanplus -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc info 2>&1 | grep -Ei "Firmware Revision" 2>&1" .
ai_packages_needed: debug-port jumper + uart_fw_py.exe + encrypted_rom.ima + UART cable (operator)
ai_logs_output: operator changes jumper, runs uart_fw_py.exe (ast2600 spi/cs, COM4) to flash encrypted_rom.ima, restores jumper and confirms the BMC flashes; agent verifies BMC responds after.
risk: RISK: changing the debug jumper + UART re-flash is destructive; operator-only with the approved encrypted ROM image.

ai_commands: -- Immediately Shutdown (GPIO): run the GPIO power-control script to immediately shutdown the system, confirm it is off, then power back on. Agent can invoke the script over SSH sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "/usr/bin/powerctrl.sh power_off 2>&1; sleep 5; /usr/bin/powerctrl.sh power_status 2>&1 2>&1" ; a hard GPIO shutdown is destructive to running state (the SSH session is cut at shutdown).
ai_packages_needed: powerctrl.sh (on the SUT) + out-of-band power path
ai_logs_output: return the power_off result + power_status so the operator confirms the command sent, the system shut down and it can be powered back on.
risk: RISK: immediate GPIO shutdown cuts all running state/SSH; use an out-of-band path and operator-approved window.

ai_commands: -- Power status (GPIO): run the GPIO power-control script to read the system power status (expected "Host Run Power Status : Good / ON"). Agent can query it sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "/usr/bin/powerctrl.sh power_status 2>&1 2>&1" , then power off and re-query to confirm it reports the low/off state.
ai_logs_output: return the power_status output in both ON and off states so the operator confirms the response data is Good/ON and then the low state when off.
risk: RISK: the second half of the check powers the system off; operator-approved window.

ai_commands: -- Power On (GPIO): while the system is in standby, run the GPIO power-control script to power it on and confirm it boots. Agent can issue the power-on over SSH, but the system must be in standby with the GPIO controller reachable sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "/usr/bin/powerctrl.sh power_on 2>&1; sleep 5; /usr/bin/powerctrl.sh power_status 2>&1; uptime 2>&1 2>&1" .
ai_logs_output: return the power_on result + power_status + uptime so the operator confirms the command sent and the system powered on and works.
risk: RISK: power-on via GPIO is a hardware action; confirm the standby state first.
